1.why: All 12 screens are static with no animations or pop-ups, though the persistent technical 'Logs' panel adds some visual clutter to an otherwise clean layout.

2.why: The current step is highlighted in dark blue in the progress bar and primary actions use large high-contrast dark-blue buttons with orange focus outlines.

3.why: Each screen presents a single labeled field and one primary button under a clear heading, though jargon labels like 'Separate possession value' may slow quick scanning.

4.why: All 7 steps are persistently displayed in the progress bar and the password rule is restated on-screen, so the user need not memorize the process, though several codes must be transcribed.

5.why: No password manager prompt, autofill hint, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: The email is prefilled at sign-in (step_08) and banners confirm restored values (e.g., 'Your simulated recovery identity value has been restored in the field'), so saved items are recognizable.

7.why: Sentences are short and typography is legible, but phrases like 'testing mock reset token', 'recovery identity value', and 'distinct possession value' are technical and unclear.

8.why: No error message appears in any of the 12 screenshots; only green success confirmations are shown, so error-message quality cannot be confirmed.

9.why: Steps include brief instructions (e.g., 'Paste or type the testing mock reset token here') but no concrete examples or sample input formats are shown.

10.why: No choice among authentication methods (e.g., password vs. code vs. face login) is offered; the flow is a single fixed sequence of password, six-digit code, and possession value.

11.why: Every screen offers only one input and one primary action at a time, so the user never faces multiple simultaneous choices.

12.why: Each action produces an explicit green outcome banner (e.g., 'Testing mock reset token confirmed', 'You are signed in', 'appointment request is confirmed').

13.why: A 'Need help?' button appears on every screen and short per-step tips are provided (e.g., 'You can pause at any time'), though the help content itself is not shown.

14.why: No error or retry state is depicted in the screenshots, but fields remain editable and there are no timeouts, so retrying appears possible though undemonstrated.

15.why: The header, progress bar, single-card layout, button styling, and confirmation-banner pattern are identical across all 12 screens.
